candidates.title: Dedicated Scheduler for Kubernetes in Robotics Applications with ROS/ROS2
candidates.abstract: A crescente complexidade dos sistemas robóticos baseados em Robot Operating System (ROS), em particular os que dependem de cargas computacionais intensivas como perceção e planeamento, tem motivado a transferência de parte do processamento do robô para recursos externos.O Kubernetes afirmou-se como a solução de referência para orquestrar aplicações em software containers, mas o seu agendador por omissão foi desenhado para cargas de trabalho genéricas: não considera requisitos de latência, classes de Quality of Service (QoS), proximidade a hardware específico, nem os padrões de comunicação próprios dos sistemas ROS.As ferramentas existentes que aproximam o ROS do Kubernetes resolvem a containerização e a orquestração, mas delegam as decisões de colocação no agendador por omissão, deixando por explorar os benefícios de um escalonamento dedicado.Esta dissertação apresenta um agendador Kubernetes dedicado a aplicações robóticas, implementado como um conjunto de dez plugins nativos do Scheduler Framework, distribuídos por cinco pontos de extensão: ordenação da fila por classe de QoS ROS, filtragem por orçamento de latência, afinidade de hardware e co-localização de dados partilhados, pontuação por topologia, latência, utilização de recursos e margem de deadline, e reserva de domínios Data Distribution Service (DDS) e de dispositivos de acesso exclusivo.O agendador é configurado de forma declarativa e integra-se no Rigel, um framework de containerização de aplicações ROS, cujo plugin de orquestração foi também migrado para suportar ROS2 no âmbito deste trabalho.Um gerador automático de perfis infere os requisitos de escalonamento a partir dos metadados que cada pacote ROS já contém.O sistema foi validado num cluster Minikube de três nós com uma suite de dez aplicações de referência.A validação funcional confirmou que todos os plugins produzem as decisões de colocação pretendidas, e a experiência quantitativa de teleoperação mostrou que o agendador dedicado iguala a qualidade de colocação do agendador por omissão sem custo de latência mensurável, garantindo em todas as colocações o orçamento de latência e o deadline declarados.O gerador de perfis inferiu corretamente a classe de QoS em três dos cinco cenários e os requisitos de hardware em todos.Estes resultados mostram que é possível aproximar a orquestração cloud-native dos requisitos das aplicações robóticas sem exigir conhecimentos de Kubernetes aos programadores de robótica.

candidates.title: Bridging the Embedded Execution Gap: A Review of the Functional Mock-up Interface for Actuator-Centric Execution Workflows in Industrial Embedded Systems
candidates.abstract: Abstract Industrial actuators integrate multi-domain physical dynamics with embedded control algorithms under strict timing constraints. Despite mature model-based design workflows, a persistent embedded execution gap separates validated high-fidelity simulation models from deterministic, resource-bounded execution on embedded industrial platforms. This review examines the Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI) as an interoperability enabler for actuator development workflows and argues that interoperability at the model-exchange level does not automatically translate into interoperability at the execution level. The review analyzes the evolution of FMI from version 2.0 to 3.0, systematizes actuator-relevant fidelity requirements (nonlinearities, compliance/resonance, timing effects), and evaluates representative approaches for integrating FMI into industrial and robotic toolchains. Two deployment trajectories are synthesized: (i) runtime-constrained FMU execution on edge/MCU-class platforms for prototyping, monitoring, and non-safety-critical functions; and (ii) analyzable code-generation paths such as Embedded FMI (eFMI) and GALEC, which target bounded memory and timing transparency for certification-oriented workflows. Although FMI 3.0 introduces improved timing semantics through clocks and Scheduled Execution, end-to-end feasibility remains limited by toolchain maturity, scheduler integration patterns, and the scarcity of complete quantitative evidence on jitter, WCET, and memory footprint under realistic load. The review identifies key challenges in determinism, fidelity management, certification alignment, and ecosystem-level conformance/validation, clarifying the technical barriers that must be addressed to fully bridge the gap between high-fidelity simulation and embedded actuator deployment.

candidates.title: Development and control of a robotic lower limb exoskeleton for pediatric users
candidates.abstract: This work presents the development of a pediatric lower limb exoskeleton (LLE) designed for passive gait rehabilitation for school-age users with motor limitations. The work focuses on the mechanical design of the device, adapted to the anthropometry of school-age users, and allows movement in six degrees of freedom (DoF) in the hip, ankle, and knee of each limb. The instrumentation includes six brushless motors, a microcontroller, and two power supplies. A sliding mode (SM) control strategy, in conjunction with a super-twisting algorithm (STA) as a robust exact differentiator, was implemented to estimate angular movements and generate gait assistance for the user. The LLE’s performance was evaluated using the normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) compared to a proportional derivative (PD) control with STA. The results show a stable, accurate control response and reduced error in joint trajectory tracking compared to PD. The SM control achieved NRMSE values of 2.39 %, 3.47 %, and 6.79 % at the hip, knee, and ankle, respectively, which were compared with the literature.

candidates.title: Storytelling and educational robotics in literature education: a quasi-experimental study
candidates.abstract: Abstract Despite the growing interest in integrating educational robotics into storytelling activities, only a few empirical studies have been conducted in the field of literature education. Accordingly, the present study examines the integration of Storytelling and Educational Robotics into the teaching of Greek literature (Homer’s Odyssey), in comparison with conventional Storytelling -based instruction. The study was conducted over 16 weeks in five public secondary schools in Greece with 227 participants aged 12–13 and employed a quasi-experimental design involving an experimental group (156 students) and a control group (71 students). The experimental group received an 8-lesson storytelling-robotics course using the DuckyCode robot. The control group received the same literary content through conventional instruction. The learning outcomes for both groups were measured on three different occasions: prior to the start of the intervention (pre-test), during the intervention (intermediate test), and after the completion of the intervention (post-test). ANCOVA and repeated-measures ANOVA indicated that students in the experimental group achieved significantly better learning outcomes compared to the control group at the intermediate and post-test measurements, with a large effect size (η²ₚ = 0.256). Furthermore, it was revealed that the students in the experimental group showed statistically significant improvement in learning outcomes over time, while the control group maintained stable learning performance. Overall, the results suggest that integrating Educational Robotics into Storytelling-based literature instruction may significantly enhance students’ learning outcomes compared to conventional Storytelling instruction alone.

candidates.title: From environmental concerns to nationalist waves: Mapping the evolving Fukushima wastewater discourse on Weibo
candidates.abstract: This study employed Structural Topic Modeling (STM) on 56,526 Weibo posts to examine the evolving discourses surrounding the Fukushima wastewater release. While rational discourse focusing on technical and environmental concerns initially coexisted and competed with nationalist narratives, the discourse rapidly transformed into predominantly nationalist rhetoric driven by grassroots users. Nationalism discourse was framed through two antagonisms: 1) direct, volatile anti-Japanese sentiment rooted in historical grievances and 2) broader, consistent anti-Western skepticism anchored in geopolitical rivalries. Moving beyond the binary paradigm of Chinese cyber-nationalism as either purely top-down mobilization or bottom-up explosion, this study reveals a nuanced interplay between actor types: grassroots users predominantly led nationalistic discourses, especially anti-Japanese discourse, while Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) focused on technical discussions but occasionally amplified anti-Western sentiment. By identifying a latent nationalist sensitivity and a victimhood-centric view of international affairs, the study demonstrates how affective public sentiment can transform environmental issues into perceived insults to national dignity, intensified by platform-mediated grassroots agency.

candidates.title: Spiritual Care as Soul Work: From Virtual Invitations to Invisible Vocations
candidates.abstract: Based in a perspective informed by contemporary depth psychology’s recognition of the need for soul and steeped in contemporary philosophical theology, this article explores potential issues with emphasizing spiritual care as a practice. Using a blend of philosophical hermeneutics and existential phenomenology to examine the contemporary crisis symptomized by virtual realities, this article unfolds in three movements that argue for the importance of soul-oriented leadership development. The first section identifies our contemporary problem as an absence of soul. It builds on Glen Slater’s recent Jung vs. Borg and explores the problems that arise when emphasizing spirit, emphasizing the difficulties with virtual reality and the onset of disconnection that results. The second section contributes one potential for resolving the problem—through an emphasis on soul-oriented leadership development. It explores Jungian psychoanalytic work with an emphasis on sound instead of sight, outlining its potential as a resource for helping leaders individuate in ways that enhance personal virtue. The resulting sense of vocation—a calling gained through listening—provides an essential framework for leadership development as a form of soul work. The third section outlines the potential for leaders to embody a sense of a radical, believing hope based in their resulting access to creative soul work. The article concludes with a statement of hope concerning how those familiar with depth psychology or spiritual care might reflect on the potential meaning of their work.

candidates.title: Zep Tepi: People Of The First Time Hypothesis - Saharan Cultural Memory and the Origins of Egyptian Sacred Symbolism
candidates.abstract: Between ~14,800 and 5,500 years ago the Sahara was green — savanna, rivers, lakes, and home to tens of thousands of pastoralists. When the African Humid Period ended abruptly, these populations followed shrinking watercourses northeast along documented paleorivers (Tamanrasset → Kufra) toward the only permanent water left: the Nile.This hypothesis proposes that these Saharan groups — carrying the ancient North African genetic lineage first documented at Taforalt (15,000 BP) and recently confirmed through Takarkori (7,000 BP) — transmitted a sophisticated symbolic and ritual package that became foundational to Predynastic Egypt and A-Group/Kerma Nubia. Central elements include: the concentric-ring + teardrop geometry of the Eye of Horus (Wedjat), already visible in the landscape of the Richat Structure (“Eye of the Sahara”) and carved at Messak Settafet ~6,000–4,000 BCE cattle cosmograms built in thousands of skulls at Kerma (~2,500–1,500 BCE) the protective “First Time” (Zep Tepi) cosmology describing a mound rising from water Supporting lines of evidence converge on a ~4,000–3,700 BCE corridor movement: published ancient DNA continuity (Taforalt → Takarkori) dairying, dung fuel, S-twist textiles, pearl millet/sorghum/weed dispersal isotopic dust signature shift in Nile sediments authenticated ancient Brucella & M. tuberculosis gradient (west → east, oldest → youngest) abrupt appearance of royal iconography (White Crown, Horus falcon) in Nubia before Egypt unifies The model generates explicit, low-cost, falsifiable tests using existing museum collections (A-Group aDNA, Richat lithology matching, cattle/crop/isotope continuity). If confirmed, it reframes Egyptian sacred symbolism not as sudden invention but as cultural memory carried across 3,000 km and ~3,000 years. If refuted, the pattern dissolves.All data and code for the novel pathogen screen are reproducible from public SRA accessions. The full 25-field synthesis, predictions, and supplementary authentication tables are openly available.
